name: Etranacogene dezaparvovec

discovery.by: Paolo Simioni and colleagues (University of Padua)
discovery.note: Discovery of the hyperactive factor IX Padua variant (R338L) in a family with thrombophilia, later used to make gene therapy more potent.

tagline: One-time AAV gene therapy delivering hyperactive factor IX for haemophilia B
summary: Etranacogene dezaparvovec is an adeno-associated virus serotype 5 vector carrying the gene for the highly active factor IX Padua variant under a liver-specific promoter. A single infusion lets the liver produce factor IX, reducing bleeding and removing the need for routine prophylaxis in most adults with haemophilia B.
mechanism: Haemophilia B results from deficiency of coagulation factor IX. The AAV5 vector delivers a codon-optimised F9 Padua transgene to hepatocytes, where it persists mainly as non-integrated episomes and is expressed under a liver-specific promoter.

The Padua variant (R338L) has roughly five to eight times the specific activity of wild-type factor IX, so modest transgene expression yields clinically useful factor IX activity, typically around 30–40% of normal in trials.
uses: Adults with haemophilia B who use factor IX prophylaxis, have current or past life-threatening haemorrhage, or have repeated serious spontaneous bleeding

history.title: Factor IX Padua
history.detail: A hyperactive factor IX variant is described in an Italian family with thrombosis.

history.title: HOPE-B trial
history.detail: uniQure begins the pivotal phase 3 trial of AMT-061.

history.title: CSL licence
history.detail: CSL Behring acquires global rights from uniQure.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Hemgenix becomes the first gene therapy for haemophilia B; its US list price of $3.5 million made it the world's most expensive medicine at the time.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Conditional marketing authorisation granted in the EU.

pk.metabolism: vector shedding in semen and blood declines over months

serious: theoretical risk of hepatocellular carcinoma from vector integration

facts: Patients with pre-existing anti-AAV5 neutralising antibodies were not excluded from HOPE-B, unlike many other AAV trials.
